title: Percent change
meaning: Percent change says how much a number grew or shrank, compared with where it started. A rise from 80 to 100 is a change of 20, and 20 is one quarter of the starting 80, so the change is 25%.
Analysts use it because a raw difference can mislead: going up by 20 is huge for a store that sold 10 last month and tiny for one that sold 10,000. Percent change puts both on the same scale.

formula.spoken: percent change equals new value minus old value, divided by old value, times 100

symbols.meaning: the change; it is negative when the value went down
turns a decimal such as 0.25 into a percent such as 25%

example.intro: A shop sold 80 mugs in May and 100 mugs in June. What is the percent change from May to June?

steps: The old value is May (80), because May comes first.
The answer is positive, so it is an increase of 25%.

Check the other way: if sales fell from 100 back to 80, the change is −20 ÷ 100 = −0.20, a decrease of 20%. Going up 25% and then down 20% gets you back where you started, because each step divides by a different old value.

trap.wrong: Dividing by the new value: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20, i.e. 20%.
trap.why: Percent change is always measured against where you started, so the old value goes on the bottom. Exam answer lists often include the divide-by-new result, so check which number you divided by before you pick.
